title: SpaceX Stock (SPCX) Falls 0.6% to $139.11 (Nov 13)
summary: SpaceX stock (SPCX) fell 0.59% to $139.11 on Nov 13, a smaller drop than the Nasdaq, before Starship Flight 15 lost its booster but had its ship caught.
body_markdown:
At the close, SPCX sat 38.35% below its 52-week high of $225.64 and 32.70% above its 52-week low of $104.83. According to[TheStreet](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/morgan-stanley-doubles-down-spacex-183300186.html) , the stock also finished about 3% above its $135[IPO](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/what-is-an-ipo/) price from June.


## Why SpaceX Stock Fell


None of the reports reviewed for this article named a SpaceX-specific cause for Friday's dip, so the move reads as part of a softer session for tech stocks rather than a reaction to company news. As reported by TheStreet, shares were around $138 by midday, with Starship Flight 15 set to launch later that day.


Per[Moneywise](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/spacex-caught-starship-orbit-robot-180500736.html) , Flight 15 lifted off from Starbase, Texas, at 5:47 p.m. ET on November 13, after the 4 p.m. close. The Super Heavy booster called off its planned tower catch, headed for the Gulf of Mexico and exploded, in the first catch attempt with the newest booster design. TheStreet reported that shares slipped in after-hours trading once the booster loss was known.


On Saturday, November 14, the tower's mechanical arms caught Ship 42 after about 22.5 hours and 14 orbits, the first catch of a spacecraft returning from orbit, according to Moneywise, which noted that Monday, November 16, is the market's first chance to react to the catch. The flight came after Bloomberg reported that[SpaceX and Tesla could announce a merger](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/tesla-tsla-stock-news-november-13-2026/) by December or early 2027, as TheStreet noted.


## SPCX Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Before its tower catch, Ship 42 released 26 Starlink V3 satellites about 35 minutes after liftoff, per Moneywise.
- SpaceX reported third-quarter revenue of $14.6 billion and earnings of $4.4 billion, according to TheStreet.


### Risks


- The Super Heavy booster was lost on the first catch attempt with its newest design, per Moneywise.
- Third-quarter capital spending was $19.6 billion, and the finance chief expects $35 billion to $40 billion in the fourth quarter, per TheStreet, after SpaceX announced more than $74 billion in Texas and Arizona data center projects on November 12.
- SpaceX is among the stocks Kalshi now offers as perpetual futures with leverage of up to 3.5 times, a product CME Chief Executive Terry Duffy warned could hurt retail investors, as reported by[Bloomberg](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/options/articles/traders-turn-kalshi-stock-perps-150000698.html) .


TheStreet expects the fourth-quarter report in early 2027; that timing is an estimate, not a confirmed date.
